raw_segments.text: The sons of Atreus called a meeting which was not as it should be, for it was sunset,
and the Achaeans were heavy with wine.
When they explained why they had called the people together, it seemed that Menelaus was
for sailing homeward at once, and this displeased Agamemnon, who thought that we should wait
till we had offered Hecatomes to appease the anger of Minerva.
Fool that he was, he might have known that he would not prevail with her, for when the
gods have made up their minds, they do not change them lightly.
So the two stood bandying hard words, whereon the Achaeans sprang to their feet with a cry
that rent the air, and were of two minds as to what they should do.
